items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4478

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the railroad law and the state finance law, in
relation to trespass on railroad property and the establishment of the
railroad crossing safety fund


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
To provide a much-needed upgrade of the railroad trespass laws to
reflect the modern security and public safety challenges facing
railroads and the public in the post 9/11 environment.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
This measure would do the following:  Section 83 of the Railroad Law
is amended to clarify existing law relating to the scope of a
railroad's liability exposure for a person trespassing on railroad
property or riding on the exterior platform of a rail car. Provisions
relating to general trespass along railroad tracks and the scope of
horse crossings are moved to new §83-c.

Section 83-a of such law is amended to make it illegal to operate any
motor vehicle or motorized recreational vehicle upon posted railroad
property or along the tracks of an operating railroad (except where
such vehicle may legally cross the tracks). Under current law, this
provision is limited to the operation of snowmobiles. A violation of
this provision shall be deemed a violation and punishable by a fine of
$100-$250.

Section 83-b of the Railroad Law relating to the adoption of local
laws in New York City and the counties of Nassau, Suffolk and Monroe
regarding trespass along railroad property is left intact. The
provision of that section providing that the trespass provisions of
the Railroad Law or any local law enacted pursuant to this section
will not preclude prosecution for trespass under the Penal Law is
moved to new §83-c.

Adds a new §83-c to the Railroad Law to bring all the general trespass
provisions together in one section.

* Subdivision (1) restates and updates the provisions moved from §83
regarding the prohibition against any person trespassing on railroad
property, its tracks or right-of-way. A violation of this subdivision
is designated as a violation punishable by a fine of $100-$250.

* Subdivision (2) of §83-c restates the restrictions relating to
leading a horse or other animal across railroad tracks previously
contained in Section 83. The penalty for any such violation is raised
from the current $10 to a sum not to exceed $100.

* Paragraph (a) of subdivision (3) makes it a misdemeanor to
knowingly, recklessly or otherwise engage in conduct that results in
damage to or defacement of railroad property. This may include such
things as throwing objects, placing objects on the tracks, defacing
equipment or interfering with signals. The offense is subject to a
monetary penalty of $500-$1500 and such other penalties as set forth
in the Penal Law. Under paragraph (b), a violation of the provisions
of paragraph (a) which disrupts, delays or in any way interferes with
railroad operations is designated as a felony (class E) punishable by
a fine of $1,000-$2,500 and such other penalties as proscribed in the
Penal Law. Additionally, anyone convicted of this provision may be
required, as a condition of sentence, to compensate an affected
railroad for any disruption, delay or interference. Under paragraph
(c), if the conduct set forth in paragraphs (a) or (b) results in the
death of or serious injury to any other person, such conduct will be

deemed to be a class D felony, punishable by a fine $2,500-55,000 and
such other penalties as set forth in the Penal Law.

* Subdivision 4 sets forth the parameters for "permission" and
"notice" as they relate to entry upon railroad property.

* Subdivision 5 provides that nothing contained in the forgoing
sections will preclude prosecution of any person for applicable
provisions of the Penal Law, including violations of the trespass
provisions pursuant to Article 140 or the assault and homicide
provisions as set forth in Articles 120 and 125 respectively.

A new section 83-d is created to provide that all fines and
forfeitures collected pursuant to the foregoing provisions (except for
compensation paid to an affected railroad) shall be deposited to the
credit of the Railroad Crossing Safety Fund.

A new section 97-eeee is added to the State Finance Law to establish
the Railroad Crossing Safety Fund. Monies in the account shall be
expended for programs to improve safety at railroad grade crossing and
along railroad right-of-way through the "Operation Life Saver"
program.  According to NYSDOT data, these types of accidents accounted
for 96% of all fatal rail accidents in the State during the past
decade.

A new section 93-c is created to establish that funds from the
Railroad Crossing Safety Fund may be used to supplement but not
supplant funding from any other source available for the Operation
Lifesaver Program.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Trespassing on railroad property has represented a danger,
predominantly to the trespassers, for as long as there have been
railroads. Indeed, the primary existing trespass provision of the
State Railroad Law (§ 83) has not been amended since it was enacted as
Chapter 481 of the Laws of 1910.

Moreover, it's original derivation can be traced to Chapter 140 of the
Laws of 1850. A few things have changed since then.

Railroad operations are certainly faster, more complex and more
sophisticated than they were in 1850 and 1910. Moreover, the
underlying safety concerns now extend well beyond the safety of the
trespasser. Now, overriding concerns with security has raised the
issue as to permissible access to the Nation's essential
transportation infrastructure. Furthermore, the population of the
state has increased while the number of motor and recreational
vehicles have skyrocketed.

For more than a century, railroads have transported freight and
passengers along dedicated lines, often carrying sensitive and
hazardous cargo safely and efficiently through the cities, towns and
villages of this nation. But, since 9/11 the consciousness of the
nation has been raised in regard to the security of the transportation
network. To that end, it is absolutely imperative that the antiquated
railroad trespass laws be amended to reflect the new public security
realities. Trespassing on railroad property cannot be tolerated; and
this legislation is but one essential component in maintaining the
integrity of the nation's rail system. As we learned from the suicidal
pick-up driver in California that caused the death of 11 rail
passengers, the consequences of even one act of trespass can be
catastrophic. Now, consider the fact that there are people who have
already intentionally used our own transportation infrastructure to
bring death and destruction to our own homeland and who will continue
to use our own technology to carry out such acts.  Additionally,
railroads are being increasingly subjected to litigation claims
brought by trespassers who enter railroad property illegally.
Accordingly, the railroad trespass laws must be updated to correspond
with the elevated threat to our public safety and security.

According to New York State DOT's Annual Rail Safety Report, trespass
accidents were by far the leading cause of fatalities in New York
State over the past decade (1994-2003), with 158 out of 201 fatalities
(79%). During this same period, there were an additional 85 trespass
related injuries. While other States, including Pennsylvania, Ohio and
Michigan, have strengthened their State trespass legislation since
9/11, New Yorkers are still subject to legislative requirements that
are 95 years old or more.

This legislation takes a firm and incremental approach to update these
laws. The concept of basic trespass is updated, but remains a
violation.  Trespass that results in damage to railroad property is a
misdemeanor.  If such action disrupts, delays or interferes with
railroad operations it shall be a felony. And, if any such action
results in the death of or serious injury to another person, it shall
be deemed a class D felony.  These penalties reflect the incremental
severity of the offense as well as the consequences of such acts.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2008: A.6809-A - Referred to Assembly Transportation Committee 2007:
A.6809 - Referred to Assembly Transportation Committee S.4732 of 2005:
Referred to Transportation S.4732 of 2006: Referred to Transportation

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None of the State Treasury, but the enhanced fines will be dedicated
to a special railway safety fund.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the first of November after which it
shall have become law.

summary: Limits railroads' liability to intruders upon their property and rights-of-way; defines offenses of trespasses on and damage to railroad property and establishes penalties therefor; also penalizes disruption of railroads and causing death or serious injury in connection therewith; establishes the railroad crossing safety fund, to be funded by fines and forfeitures from railroad-related offenses; the fund is to be used for training and education to improve safety at railroad grade crossings and along railroad rights-of-way throughout the state.
title: Defines offenses of trespasses on and damage to railroad property
